# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried, and whether it moved val: (RESULT pending — harness scores after STOP.) The search strategy this iteration: read ALL 10 traces + policy + tools.py + db.json directly (serial, no fan-out — 10 traces is small), then decompose the 7 failures into ROOT-CAUSE clusters and rank by leverage = (confidence a tool edit fixes it) × (blast-radius safety). Highest-leverage class turned out to be COMMUNICATE-only failures where the DB write was already correct (task 11): these are near-deterministic to flip by RETURNING the exact figure the agent must speak, rather than letting a mid-tier model hand-compute it. This "enriched return" edit class is the single best lever found for this domain because reward_basis=[DB,COMMUNICATE] and the tool name is not graded.
- Plateau/stall signal, if any: n/a (iteration 1). But a STRUCTURAL ceiling was identified: 2 of 7 failures (40, 22) are narrated-then-user-STOP — the user simulator ends the episode with "yes###STOP###" before the agent can execute. No tool edit can manufacture a turn that never occurs, so those are un-winnable from the tool surface. That caps the realistically-reachable val at ~5/10 (0.500) from tools alone this run; the remaining 2 need a prompt/policy capability or a harness change.
- What to try next iteration: (1) If task 11 flipped, GENERALIZE the payment_summary/exact-figure-return pattern to every comm-graded numeric (booking totals, baggage charges, cancellation refunds) — it is the proven mechanism. (2) Do NOT spend iterations on 40/22 via tools; escalate to FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS instead. (3) For id-guessing (17/22), measure whether find_reservation actually gets CALLED by the mid-tier model — if not, the lever is discoverability (name/doc), not a new capability. (4) Avoid decision-rule loosening (task 17 refuse) entirely: unbounded regression risk on unseen passing cases.
